__comment__: EconomyX — phone hold poses. ONE file drives all 26 phones, because every
phone geometry uses a single bone named 'phone'.
WHY POSITION Y IS ~22.5 AND NOT 0
The geometry's root bone is bound to the hand with
"binding": "q.item_slot_to_bone_name(context.item_slot)"
and that binding is what attaches the handset to the player at all. But
Bedrock then applies a -1.5 metre (-24 unit) offset to a bound attachable,
so a model authored around the origin lands down at the player's feet. The
+24 here cancels that offset out.
The remaining -1.48 centres the handset. The geometry runs y=-5.28..+11.22,
so its centre sits at y=+2.97; at scale 0.5 that is 1.48 units, subtracted
so the MIDDLE of the phone lands on the hand rather than its lower third.
24  -  (2.97 x scale)  =  position Y
WHICH WAY DOES IT FACE
In all 9 models the camera-bump cubes sit at negative Z, so -Z is the BACK
and +Z is the SCREEN. In item-bone space -Z points the way the holder faces,
so the cameras point out at everyone else and the screen back at the holder.
The Y rotation of 35 turns that into a three-quarter view: mostly screen,
with one edge showing, so it reads as a solid object rather than a flat
plane. Set Y to 0 for dead-on, or to -35 to mirror which edge you see.
TUNING — edit ONLY this file; nothing else references these numbers.
sitting at the feet again .......... position[1] lost its +24
floating above the hand ............ lower position[1]
hanging below the hand ............. raise position[1]
too big or too small ............... change scale, then redo the sum above
wrong edge toward you .............. negate rotation[1]
you see the cameras, not the screen  add 180 to rotation[1]
